candidate_claims.text: NRI View Point cartoon My Space Reviews Education Today Property Lifestyle Home | News | Case Filed Against 15 Msf Sfi Activists For Allegedly Trampling Pm Modis Photograph In Palakkad Case filed against 15 MSF, SFI activists for allegedly trampling PM Modi’s photograph in Palakkad Police in Kerala's Palakkad district have booked around 15 MSF and SFI student activists for allegedly tearing and trampling a photograph of Prime Minister Narendra Modi during a college union election campaign event at MES Kalladi College in Mannarkkad.

By PTI Published Date - 22 October 2026, 11:15 AM Palakkad (Keralam): A case has been registered against around 15 student members of the MSF and the SFI for allegedly tearing up and trampling a photograph of Prime Minister Narendra Modi during the finale of a college union election campaign in Mannarkkad here, officials said on Thursday.

According to police, the incident occurred on October 13 around 4.30 pm in front of MES Kalladi College during the final campaign event (kottikkalasam) for the college union election, where Muslim Students Federation (MSF) and Student Federation of India (SFI) activists had gathered.

The accused allegedly tore down the Prime Minister’s photograph, threw it on the ground and trampled upon it, with the intention of provoking a public riot, the FIR said The case was registered at Mannarkkad police station under Section 192 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), for wantonly doing an illegal act with the intent or knowledge that it is likely to provoke a riot.
The case was registered on the basis of a complaint by BJP leader Biju of Mannarkkad, police added.

candidate_claims.text: Friends, You have given 1.4 billion countrymen an opportunity to feel proud.
You have enhanced the pride of the Tiranga, you have increased its honour.
And especially our women’s hockey team, you ended a long wait of 44 years by bringing home the gold medal.
In cricket, both our teams won medals for the second consecutive time and, in fact, repeated their own record.

Outstanding performances in shooting, major successes in boxing and wrestling, new records in athletics, a medal in weightlifting after twenty-eight years, and India’s success in marathon events for the first time since 1982.
Out of the 85 medals won by India, 38 medals were won by our women athletes.
Among them were 11 gold medals as well.
In Mixed Martial Arts, Soft Tennis, and certain sailing events, our players created new history by winning medals for the first time.
Friends, Over the past 12 years, India too has worked with great patience and dedication on its sportspersons and its sports ecosystem.
There used to be huge events such as the Olympics, yet India had no representation in more than half of the sports.
Over the past 10–12 years, the country worked continuously with dedication and sincerity, pursued a long-term vision, and built a transparent and modern ecosystem for sports.
As all of you know, we launched the Target Olympic Podium Scheme (TOPS).
We launched the Khelo India Scheme.
As Mansukh Bhai mentioned earlier, more than ₹36,000 crore has been allocated for expanding Khelo India and strengthening sports federations.
Friends, Today, more than one thousand Khelo India Centres have been established across the country.
Stadiums, mini-stadiums, and multi-purpose sports halls have been created.
Athletics tracks, football grounds, hockey grounds, swimming pools, and thousands of such sports infrastructures are being built in both small and large cities.
Under this scheme, direct assistance is being provided to athletes as well.

items.title: PM’s speech during the launch of development projects in Ladakh via Video Conferencing

candidate_claims.text: “Ladakh si Mi-Mangs Kunla, Jullay!” Today, another chapter is being added to the progress and development of Ladakh.
This terminal, built at a cost of about six hundred and fifty crore rupees, will increase the airport’s annual passenger capacity from one million to three and a half million.
About two thousand five hundred crore rupees have been spent on it.
A journey that earlier took around twelve hours can now be completed in approximately three hours.
Friends, Today, forty reservoirs built under Project Amrit Him Sarovar have also been dedicated to the people of Ladakh.
Until 2019, Ladakh had about 1,800 kilometres of road network.
Today, it has increased to more than 4,000 kilometres.
Today, their number has increased to about seventy-five.
The number of helipads has also increased from seven to more than forty.
Earlier, only about three and a half percent of houses in Ladakh had access to tap water.
Today, nearly 99 percent of homes have access to tap water.
The number of beds in Ladakh’s hospitals has also doubled.
Once completed, it will provide Ladakh with improved year-round connectivity to the rest of the country.
Under the Vibrant Villages Programme, the central government and we are developing more than forty border villages in Ladakh, and we call them the “first villages” of India.
Friends, Earlier, Ladakh had around one hundred and fifty homestays.
Today, their number has increased to three thousand.
These have created new possibilities for increasing farmers’ incomes.
Therefore, a major Centre of Excellence is being established in Leh.
The youth here have created a distinct identity in areas such as ice hockey, winter sports, and mountaineering.
You already know that whenever I meet foreign guests, I often present products made in Ladakh as gifts and also tell them about all of you.
Future generations will be able to understand this heritage, and visitors from around the world will also become acquainted with Ladakh’s rich history.

candidate_promises.text: Through these projects, travel will become easier for many people, electricity facilities will improve in some places, water availability will increase in others, and the conservation of our ancient heritage will also receive new strength.
This will make both administration and the justice system more accessible.
These will create better opportunities for higher education, research, and advanced skills for the youth of Ladakh within their own region.
Friends, I am confident that together we will take Ladakh to new heights of development.

items.title: PM’s address at the Bloomberg New Economy Forum in New Delhi

candidate_claims.text: Excellencies, delegates from around the world, leaders from business and industry, policymakers, and my friends.
Reflecting on his 30-year journey, he mentioned that I am his friend.
Friends, This year’s Bloomberg Economic Forum is focused on the new powers emerging around the world.
But in the 21st century, especially in this third decade, a major transformation is taking place.
India has more than one hundred languages, nearly eighty thousand registered newspapers and publications, and more than one thousand satellite television channels.
And not only that, in this age of social media, India has more than five hundred million YouTube users and more than five hundred million Instagram users.
Friends, Until about twelve or thirteen years ago, there was a time in India when access to mobile phones and the internet itself was a form of power.
After 2014, when a new government came to power in India and we were given the opportunity to serve, India placed great emphasis on making mobile data affordable.
In other words, connectivity in India has not merely connected people; it has connected opportunities as well.
Before 2014, India had only a few hundred startups.
Today, the country has more than 250,000 startups.
Nearly half of these startups come from small cities and towns.
More than forty-five percent of startups have at least one woman Director or Partner.
In other words, opportunities for innovation are reaching more people, new talent is emerging, and new solutions are being created.
Following this path, India has lifted 250 million people out of poverty over the past decade, a number greater than the population of many countries in the world.
Friends, You may also have heard about the JAM Trinity and Direct Benefit Transfer.
By using technology, we have created a system through which government assistance reaches beneficiaries directly in their bank accounts.
This has reduced corruption, increased convenience for citizens, and established a direct pathway between the government and the people.
We supplied vaccines to more than one hundred countries.
Nandan, who is seated here, can later share much more information about how this was done.
India achieved this milestone in November 2021 itself, nine years ahead of schedule.
This was not merely about fulfilling a commitment; it was also a reflection of India’s evolving energy journey.
Friends, In 2014, India’s renewable energy capacity stood at about 75 gigawatts.
Today, it has reached approximately 300 gigawatts.
In other words, we have added nearly four times more capacity.

candidate_promises.text: In 2015, we set ourselves the target of achieving 40 percent of our installed electricity capacity from non-fossil fuel sources by 2030.
